title: create-github-app-token steps must set non-empty owner and repositories
answers: create-github-app-token missing repositories or owner policy denial
GitHub App token must be scoped to a repository
why does conftest deny actions/create-github-app-token without repository scope
how do I limit a GitHub App installation token to specific repos in a workflow
body:
Invariant: every `actions/create-github-app-token` step in a workflow must set a non-empty `with.owner` and a non-empty `with.repositories`, so the issued token is narrowed to named repositories.
Enforced by .github/policy.rego:deny_create_app_token_without_repository_scope, which denies a missing, empty or whitespace-only value for either key and names the job and missing key in the message.
Existing uses follow the pattern: .github/workflows/uv.yml, flaky-test-detector.yml and ui-review.yml set `owner: mlflow` and `repositories: mlflow` next to the `permission-*` inputs.
What breaks if skipped: the conftest policy check fails for that workflow; removing either input produces the matching denial.
Constraints: the rule walks input.jobs through job_steps, so steps that live only in composite action.yml files are not checked by it. It checks presence only, not whether the repository names are valid.
applies: Any workflow step using actions/create-github-app-token in this repo; check the policy rule's coverage before relying on it for composite actions.
says: Security policy checks fail when generating a GitHub App token without specifying repositories.
Workflow checks reject application tokens that lack explicit repository and organization scoping.
How do I scope an automated application token to specific repositories for policy approval?
Prevent security policy rejections by explicitly naming the target repositories for application tokens.
Automated workflow validation denies token generation steps that omit target repository restrictions.
search: Every actions/create-github-app-token step in a workflow must specify non-empty with.owner and with.repositories inputs to restrict the token to named repositories. This invariant is enforced by .github/policy.rego:deny_create_app_token_without_repository_scope, which fails conftest policy checks if either key is missing, empty, or whitespace-only. The rule inspects job steps directly, meaning composite action files are not evaluated and valid repository names are not verified.
